doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: House bassist on Prestige and Blue Note dates, and gigs with Ben Webster
summary: Heath explains he paid his rent by recording for Prestige and Blue Note with Art Farmer, Horace Silver and Milt Jackson, and mentions Ben Webster at Bowman's.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Wasn’t the Jazztet later? I thought the Jazztet was formed like in 1959. But there was a Jazztet…
But then it was before Art Farmer…
He was with Lionel Hampton with…
He left Hampton and made a record for Prestige on a sextet or something…
Quincy Jones was on those records?

Yeah, I made those records. But anyhow, I made records with almost everybody back there who was recording for Prestige, and that’s how I made my rent actually. ‘Cause by then we had moved up in Harlem River Drive in those new apartments up above the Polo Grounds. It was a middle-income deal up there, and that was the bracket I was in at that time. And during that time, I worked with Ben Webster up at a place called Bowman’s, up 155th Street, right near Coogan’s Bluff, between 8th Avenue and Coogan’s Bluff right on the hill there. Ben Webster, Duke Jordan and a drummer, Arthur Edgehill, we were playing up there behind Phil Black, who was a female impersonator and a shake dancer, it was a real wild gig, but that’s when Ben Webster, we fell in love with each other, up at Bowman’s. He incidentally had once gave me a gig with the Duke Ellington cats…

No, it was with Johnny Hodges and Sonny Greer. Boy, we had a good time on that gig. That was the only time I played with the Duke Ellington guys. But during that period, like becoming a house bass player, so to speak, for Blue Note and Prestige, the jazz labels, I recorded with an awful lot of people, including Monk and Miles and this discography, I can’t even recall who I recorded with. It was Horace Silver’s first date…
And some of Milt Jackson’s dates, and that was how I paid my rent making record dates. I think it was about $55 a sessions, or something like that, for a three-hour session.
